## Why This Is Asked
This tests practical ability to implement auditable patch management for SAP on AWS, a common, beginner-friendly operational task.

## Key Concepts
- AWS Systems Manager maintenance windows, Run Command, and State Manager
- DynamoDB as an audit ledger for approvals
- Health checks and rollback automation

## Code Example
```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  PatchRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: [ssm.amazonaws.com, ec2.amazonaws.com]
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      Path: '/'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: PatchPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: ['ssm:*', 'ec2:Describe*', 'dynamodb:*']
                Resource: '*'
  MaintWindow:
    Type: AWS::SSM::MaintenanceWindow
    Properties:
      Name: SAPPatchWindow
      Schedule: 'cron(0 2 ? * SUN *)'
      AllowUnassociatedTargets: true
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical automation skills for SAP HANA backup reliability, emphasizing serverless event-driven verification, durable state management, and timely alerting mechanisms.

## Key Concepts
- S3 versioning with encrypted backup storage
- Lambda event-driven processing on S3 PUT operations
- Backup integrity verification using cryptographic checksums
- Durable result storage via DynamoDB
- Automated alerting through SNS or CloudWatch

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudocode: verify backup integrity
function verifyBackup(backupKey) {
  const actual = computeChecksum(backupData);
  const expected = getExpectedChecksum(backupKey);
  
  const result = {
    backupKey,
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    status: actual === expected ? 'verified' : 'failed',
    actualChecksum: actual,
    expectedChecksum: expected
  };
  
  // Record in DynamoDB for durability
  dynamoDB.put(result);
  
  // Alert on failures
  if (result.status === 'failed') {
    sns.publish({
      message: `Backup integrity check failed for ${backupKey}`,
      subject: 'SAP HANA Backup Alert'
    });
  }
  
  return result;
}
```

## CloudFormation Example
```yaml
Resources:
  BackupVerificationRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: SAP-HANA-BackupVerificationRole
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: S3AccessPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - s3:GetObject
                  - s3:GetObjectVersion
                Resource: arn:aws:s3:::your-backup-bucket/*
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - s3:ListBucket
                  - s3:GetBucketVersioning
                Resource: arn:aws:s3:::your-backup-bucket
        - PolicyName: DynamoDBAccessPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - dynamodb:PutItem
                  - dynamodb:GetItem
                Resource: arn:aws:dynamodb:*:*:table/backup-verification-results
        - PolicyName: SNSAccessPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - sns:Publish
                Resource: arn:aws:sns:*:*:backup-alerts
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses practical knowledge of enterprise patch governance across multiple AWS accounts for SAP workloads running on EC2. It tests understanding of AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager, cross-account access patterns, and automated compliance monitoring.

## Key Concepts
- AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager for automated patching
- Cross-account IAM roles with trust policies
- Patch baselines and approval rules
- Maintenance windows for scheduled patching
- CloudWatch alarms for compliance monitoring
- AWS Config and SSM compliance reports for auditing

## Minimal IaC Snippet (CloudFormation)

```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Cross-account patch management resources

Resources:
  CrossAccountRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: ssm-patch-manager-role
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: arn:aws:iam::SHARED_ACCOUNT_ID:root
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore

  SAPPatchBaseline:
    Type: AWS::SSM::PatchBaseline
    Properties:
      Name: sap-weekly-patch-baseline
      OperatingSystem: AMAZON_LINUX_2
      ApprovalRules:
        Rules:
          - PatchFilterGroup:
              PatchFilters:
                - Key: MSRC_SEVERITY
                  Values: [Critical, Important]
                - Key: CLASSIFICATION
                  Values: [SecurityUpdates, BugfixUpdates]
            PatchSet: AWS_DEFAULT
            ApproveAfterDays: 7
      Description: Weekly SAP OS patch baseline for critical and important updates
```
